single_xeno.consistency_note: N/A -- single sequential run, no concurrent duplication possible

independent_n_no_s1.consistency_note: no shared state exists to prevent it, so every node redoes every task independently -- with GRID10's claim-awareness the same 4 tasks require exactly 4 generations total, not up to 40

naive_voting.note: produces one answer to one pre-chosen question via majority; has no mechanism at all for multi-task claim-awareness, hyperposition preservation, or persistent cross-task state -- those concepts do not apply to this architecture, which is exactly the gap GRID10's S1 fabric closes

fixed_random_coordinator.note: unlike GRID10 (criterion coordinator_failure_replacement=PASS, a healthy node is automatically re-elected via elect_coordinator's healthy-node scan), a fixed/random-once coordinator has no re-election call anywhere in this design by construction -- a dead fixed coordinator permanently strands its scope's Result-Channel backlog

compression_lesion.note: branch:a and branch:b both accumulate real committed results, but with recursive compression skipped there is no GLOBAL view at all -- a consumer asking 'what has the whole fabric learned' gets nothing, even though the per-scope work genuinely happened; this is the direct contrast to GRID10's recursive_global_compression=PASS criterion

dynamic_coordinator.note: = the actual physical GRID10 acceptance run itself (11 real fork()'d processes, 17/17 criteria PASS)
dynamic_coordinator.coordinator_failure_replacement: PASS -- contrast directly with fixed_random_coordinator's stuck=true above
dynamic_coordinator.recursive_global_compression: PASS -- contrast directly with compression_lesion's cross_scope_visibility=false above

hyperposition_lesion.note: this is REAL evidence, not simulated: the first two physical GRID10 acceptance runs (before grid10_node.py was patched to carry `unresolved_alternatives` through NODE_RESULT) both produced hyperposition_preservation.pass=false -- found_paris=false, found_minority_alt=false -- because the node's cognitive_answer() collapsed the task to its own single greedy answer and silently dropped the declared alternatives. That IS the lesioned behavior; the fix (see commit history on tools/grid10_node.py) is what makes the current GRID10_ACCEPTANCE_RECEIPT.json show hyperposition_preservation.pass=true.

headline.correctness: single_xeno and dynamic_coordinator both achieve full task correctness on this small set; naive_voting depends entirely on majority luck for the ONE question it can even ask; fixed_random_coordinator and compression_lesion show real committed work becoming permanently stuck/invisible once their missing mechanism is needed
headline.efficiency: independent_n_no_s1 wastes 36/40 generations (90%) doing the exact same 4 tasks 10 times over with no claim-awareness -- GRID10's claim-awareness criterion (PASS) is what prevents this
headline.resilience: only dynamic_coordinator (GRID10) survives a coordinator dying (coordinator_failure_replacement=PASS); fixed_random_coordinator strands its scope permanently
headline.structural_completeness: only dynamic_coordinator (GRID10) provides both cross-scope visibility (recursive_global_compression) and preserves genuinely unresolved alternatives (hyperposition_preservation) -- every challenger config is missing at least one of these by construction, not by bad luck
